And I told Mr. Blagoje that I would like if the Crisis Staff found that appropriate, to go and see Mr. Slobodan Skripinja, about whom I knew at the time, that he was performing the function of the main chief of the service at the level of Republika Srpska, at the ministry of internal affairs. That is why I wanted to go and discuss this question with him there, instead of being appointed by a municipal body, and I wanted to see how to organise this service, because one person could not represent the whole service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zaric, you asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Pardon. Excuse me. If I may put a question to the accused Mr. Blagoje Simic. What do you answer to this, what has been said by Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. He cannot answer. Can Mr. Pisarevic just continue with the evidence of your client.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When you acquainted Mr. Blagoje Simic with this problem and told him that this couldn't be done in this way, what did Mr. Blagoje Simic tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Blagoje Simic told me that he had the best intentions with this decisions, but that he would take into account my remarks, and he said that at the first next scheduled meeting, or at one of the following Crisis Staff meetings, he would put the question of me going to Pale and conducting this conversation and then report back to him about that, and that is how we ended our conversation on the topic of this decision which I had received.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever begin to carry out the duties of chief for national security, based on this decision that you were given?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I never started to perform this job, nor did I ever think of doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out, or were you present at the next meeting of the Crisis Staff? Did you find out whether this was an item that was discussed on the agenda, and were you present?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After seven or ten days, at the most - I can't remember exactly - there was a meeting of the Crisis Staff, to which I was invited, and one of the items on the agenda, under various, was the proposal for Mr. Zaric to go to Pale in order to agree on how to organise this national service. This is what I'm thinking. One of the items of the agenda, under miscellaneous, was the departure of Mr. Zaric to Pale in order to consult about how to organise the national security service. That was more or less how it was formulated on the agenda when I came to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you only attend when this item of the agenda was discussed, or were you present for the whole meeting of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came in as the session was already in progress, and as soon as I came inside, then this item of the agenda was brought to the table for discussion. So I didn't attend the meeting to hear what was going on before or after this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And what was the discussion of the Crisis Staff? Was this decision invalidated or withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that when Mr. Blagoje Simic brought this item to the agenda, the first person to speak was Mr. Stevan Todorovic, who was at the meeting, and I can say that I remember very well that besides him, Mr. Milos Bogdanovic was also present at the meeting, Bozo Ninkovic also, Simeon Simic, Milan Simic, Savo Popovic, Mitar Mitrovic. So it was a Crisis Staff meeting with many of its members present. That's what I would say. After this item was placed for discussion, the first person to ask to speak was Stevan Todorovic. First he attacked the Crisis Staff a little bit about how it was possible for such a decision to be adopted without his participation. I didn't have any idea that Mr. Todorovic was not present when this decision was adopted and when the Crisis Staff was discussing or making this decision. Then he focused in his discussion by addressing those present. He was sitting opposite me, and he said that he was deeply disappointed in the reflex and in the political sense of the people from the Crisis Staff and that they could name such a person to such a post, a person such as Simo Zaric. You know very well -- so I'm continuing Mr. Todorovic's story. You know very well that Mr. Simo Zaric, until yesterday, arrested people from the SDS, that the Serbian people do not have any confidence in him, in this municipality, he has no authority, and I think that you adopted a decision which makes no sense at all. It's not important what I replied to Mr. Todorovic then, but I have to say that Mr. Milos Bogdanovic and the president himself, Blagoje Simic, calmed the situation down. I just said to President Simic that I do not want to attend any more meetings of the Crisis Staff, nor do I want my name to be mentioned in any kind of context or any function or any decision of the Crisis Staff which it would need to adopt regarding this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, was this service formed after this, and was anybody appointed as chief of national security in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that later the decision was implemented, but in accordance with the methodology that I mentioned, and that was legal, through the appropriate department of the ministry of internal affairs of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I know that Mr. Ratko Mihajlovic was later appointed as chief of national security, and there were two or three other people who were performing that function. So that's how that service was covered. I didn't interfere any more, and I wasn't interested in who proposed him, but later I heard that the decision on his appointment came from the relevant department of the ministry of internal affairs of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When this decision existed, so from the 29th of April, so for those ten days or so when the decision was in force, what did you practically do?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was carrying out the duties of assistant commander of the 4th Detachment for intelligence and security and for moral affairs. This is the same job that I was performing up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, during May 1992, did you participate in the drafting of a list of Serbs who remained in the village of Trnjak after the outbreak of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you did about that list, who gave you that task, how did this come about?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there is no need for me to give any explanation, because this Honourable Trial Chamber has heard what happened to the Serbs, the Serbian people, after the 19th, when the forces of the HVO took power in that region. A large number of citizens of Serb ethnicity from my village, the village of Trnjak, where I was born, experienced the same fate as the citizens of Nova Dubica, Donji Grad, Lipik, Svilaj, and practically those places inhabited by Serbs, which means that some were taken to camps, others were taken to isolation in Novi Grad and isolation in Trnjak. The question was initiated to actually compile a list of people who were in those villages so that we would approximately know how many people were placed in camps and isolation in the region of the Odzak municipality. This question was initiated by the Red Cross, and a working group was formed - that's how I would call it - in which Mr. Bozo Ninkovic participated, who was born in Donja Dubica. That's the neighbouring village, the village next to mine. And Mr. Miroslav Tadic, who is from the biggest Serbian village in the region of the Odzak municipality, and that is Novi Grad, and of course myself, and I am from Trnjak. We were given the task, according to what we remember and from conversations with people from that area, to make a list, an accurate list, as much as that was possible, of the people who lived in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you make that list, according to what the people from Trnjak remembered?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made that list, because I went to Trnjak often, so I remembered a lot, and I used many of the inhabitants of Trnjak, whom I spoke about. They helped me. I made a list of 302 persons, and I handed this list to the Red Cross of the Bosanski Samac municipality so that they could process it further and work on it with the International Red Cross and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were how many people on the list?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there were 332 persons on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps it would be good for Mr. Zaric just to clarify. He said after the 19th. Perhaps he should tell us the month. Maybe that is not disputable, but it's still better for it to be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, you heard Mr. Lukic's suggestion.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces of the HVO, comprising of Croat and Muslim forces in the territory of the Odzak municipality, took over entire control over the municipality on the 19th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zaric. Mr. Zaric, I would now like to move on and talk about an event that took place in the village of Crkvina, in fact, the crime that occurred in the village of Crkvina. Could you tell us: When you learned of the crime that had occurred in Crkvina, when the crime happened, who told you about it, where, and who was with you at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime happened in the village of Crkvina in the night between the 8th and the 9th of May, 1992. On that day, in the evening, I was with my driver, Toso Tutnjevic. First in the command of the 17th Tactical Group, in Mr. Makso Simeunovic's office, having talks with him to transmit the usual sort of information, and then we dropped in to see a friend of mine, Rado Lukic, in Obudovac, and we stayed a little after midnight. After that, we set out via Gornja Slatina and Crkvina in the direction of Bosanski Samac. This was more or less our regular route when going to Pelagicevo and back. At the crossroads in Crkvina, we were stopped by a policeman whose name is a Sasa Maslic, and he was born in Bosanski Samac, but he was working as a policeman at that crossroads, conducting some sort of check. When he saw that Toso and I were in the car, and Sasa knew me very well, he said the following: Uncle Simo, a terrible crime has taken place in Crkvina. That man Lugar, from Serbia, has killed 16 people in the cooperative warehouse not far from the club. Sasa Maslic seemed very excited, frightened, upset, and I said: What's the situation now? What's happening? And he said that Lugar had given orders to some people that certain vehicles should be provided at once and some sort of equipment, and that these people should be taken in the direction of the River Bosna, which is about two or three kilometres away as the crow flies, some sort of crane. I asked Sasa Maslic: Has the police been here? Does anyone know anything about this? Sasa said that the commander of the police in Crkvina, Ranko Popovic, who was guarding that warehouse, when he heard that Lugar was coming, drunk as he was, Lugar, he told the policeman to take cover and not to give the key to anyone, not to let anyone in. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, just a moment. You said those persons. Did you mean those who were killed?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And we have another little problem. You said that Ranko Popovic was guarding that warehouse. Was that the warehouse where the people were detained and where the crime took place?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. Ranko Popovic was the person tasked by the police station to guard the warehouse where those people were detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you receive any other information from Sasa Maslic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He told me he had noticed that several hours before he had seen Mr. Blagoje Simic, the president of the Crisis Staff, passing by and that he assumed he was still there in Crkvina, or maybe he had gone to Kruskovo Polje to visit his parents, because there's a road leading to Kruskovo Polje from there, where he had his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say he was going to the command, what command was that?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Detachment, and the commander was Marko Tubakovic, the gentleman who testified here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, where was the command of the 2nd Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 2nd Detachment was in Gornja Crkvina, in the hamlet of Starcevici. That's what it's called, probably because some families by that name live in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How far was this command from the centre of the village where this warehouse was, the warehouse was in the centre of the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was perhaps 50 or 70 metres away from the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And what was the distance between the place where the crime took place and the headquarters of the command in the hamlet of Starcevici in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my estimation, to reach that place by car, you need to drive two or two and a half kilometres. It's at least two kilometres, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you and Toso Tutnjevic go to the command of the 2nd Detachment in Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to the command. When we arrived near the command, we were stopped by a guard who was guarding the command. He knew me by sight. And I asked if Mr. Blagoje was in the command, and he said he was there. And I said I needed to go there, so he escorted me as far as the command, which was some hundred metres away, down a path from the place where he had met us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And when you got to the house where the command was, did you enter the command?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I greeted the people inside. This was in a private house, a family house, and there was a big living room there. There were some mattresses lying around, and some people were sleeping, some were dozing, and Mr. Blagoje was with a group of people from the command and they were talking. In my estimation, this was at around 1.00 or 2.00 a.m., approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, Mr. Zaric, who else was there besides Blagoje Simic in that command?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was the commander, Marko Tubakovic, as far as I can remember; there was Mirko Vasiljevic; there was Rade Gunjevic, Joco Micic, Cvijetin Maslic. These were people I knew. There was a certain Cedo, who was in charge of radio communications, and I know him because he later worked in the post office in Crkvina. So those were the people whom I know for certain were then with Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And who did you address then, and how, when you entered the command?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I entered the command and said "good evening, how are you," they said "very well." I asked: Any news? And they said no. This was what we usually said when we saw each other. And then I realised that they really had no idea as to what had happened in their village, only about two kilometres away. So I said: Blagoje, I have to tell you something. Can you come outside?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you and Mr. Blagoje Simic go out of that room?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Blagoje and I went out in front of the building, and then I said to him: Blagoje, do you know what that fool Lugar has done in Crkvina? Mr. Simic said to me, quite surprised: No. What did he do? Well, I said, he killed people. I've just come from the crossroads, where I heard that he'd killed 16 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And how did Mr. Blagoje Simic receive this information? How did he react?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje said: Curse them. What are they doing to us? What are they doing to us? He was amazed. That's how Mr. Blagoje Simic reacted when I told him what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you agree on what steps you would take? Did you exchange any ideas about this?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said to Blagoje: This is the last straw. I'm going to inform my commander about this, to tell them what has happened. And Blagoje said: Well, I'm going right away to the Crisis Staff to do something about this. And that was all we said. I went to inform the command, and he said he was going to inform the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And after these words, did you separate?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We parted ways. But I did go back into the office with Blagoje for only a few minutes, and I said to the people that a crime had happened. I told them what had happened and they were all amazed. I said: I have things to do. Goodbye. Blagoje remained there with them. I left. I don't know when Blagoje set out in the direction of Samac, because I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you and Toso Tutnjevic then drive to the command in Samac, and what route did you take?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went by way of Pisari, taking a short cut. We passed by a farm, and very soon we arrived in the command of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who did you find in the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found Commander Antic and Savic [as interpreted]. They were both asleep, but there was a duty officer, Nikolic, and also the communications officer, and they were both awake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, my colleagues tell me that it says here that Antic and Savic were both commanders. Who was the commander in May?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Jovo Savic in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you find someone else there?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who was not the commander then?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was a slip of the tongue. But on that evening, he was in the command of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course. And did you tell Jovo Savic, Radovan Antic, and the others what had happened?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told them right away. They were all flabbergasted. Sasa Maslic in Crkvina had told me the names of some of the people who had been killed in Crkvina, and those were people I respected and liked, and others knew their names as well. They were our fellow citizens from the town of Samac, whom we knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Zaric. Can you mention for the Trial Chamber the people from Samac whom you know and who were killed in Crkvina on the 8th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of my best friends, Mr. Josip Orsolic, a schoolmate of mine, who was previously the chief of the public security station in Bosanski Samac. My son Mirel and his son Latko [phoen] went to school together so this was a long standing friendship. Ivo Tuzlak was also killed, who worked in the secretariat for National Defence of the municipality of Samac. A man called Hurtic a neighbour, who lived not far from the house where my wife was born, whom I knew personally. A man called Agatic, whom I also knew. And there were some people from Hasici, and I learned later that there were also some people from outside the municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Zaric, did you invite anyone from the command, or did you call anyone from the command of the 4th Detachment to tell them what had happened in Crkvina that evening?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I informed, over the radio, and in Pelagicevo. It was Mr. Makso Simeunovic who responded to the call. He was the first one who picked up the telephone, and I told him, very briefly - I mean Mr. Makso Simeunovic - what had happened, and I said that the Commander Nikolic should be informed urgently and that we should see what could be done about this gang.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did Makso Simeunovic tell you something at that moment?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said: Well, the commander just happens to be right here beside me. He's awake, so why don't you tell Mr. Nikolic directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And did Mr. Nikolic, the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, speak on the phone?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic picked up the receiver and I told him very briefly what had happened, and I said that we should take all possible measures because this was really the last straw. And he said to me: Please collect as much information as you can and come and see me in the command as early as possible tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you, Mr. Zaric, go to the command of the 17th Tactical Group in Pelagicevo on the following morning?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at 8.00 I was already reporting in the command of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How did you go from Samac to Pelagicevo? What means of transport did you use? And did anyone go to the command in Pelagicevo with you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went with Mr. Toso Tutnjevic. He drove me there. And together we arrived in the command of the 17th Tactical Group. I wish to add that as Sasa Maslic had told me that when this crime was committed, there was Mr. Lugar, and I heard later that Tralja was are was there, and Stanisic, also known as Ziga, and two girls, so before I went to Pelagicevo, I stopped off in Slatina and found Mr. Lazar Stanisic and heard more details from him directly, which helped me to tell about the event that had happened in Crkvina, to tell my commander, Nikolic, about it, in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And what did you and Commander Nikolic talk about when you reported to him in the command of the 17th Tactical Group in the morning? What was the date?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 9th of May, today, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So what did you talk about with Commander Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed him of everything I knew at that moment, that 16 men had been killed, that in Crkvina there were over 50 people who had been taken to that warehouse, that the warehouse had been guarded by the police, that Lugar ordered that the door be broken down and that he had killed those men. I told him very briefly what had happened. I said that he gave the order to have the people dragged off and buried somewhere near the River Bosna, which is about two or three kilometres away from the scene of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, is it time to finish for today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We have come to the end of our proceedings for today. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
